name: Remi Douangpanya
aliases: No aliases — refuses them on principle
role: Protest coordinator and direct action organizer
location: Mexicantown Libre, living communally in a building called the Stack, near Ashland and Division
description:
Remi Douangpanya is young and loud about it — she has the particular energy of someone who has concluded that patience is a trap laid by people who benefit from delay. She is dark-skinned and angular, with natural hair grown into a dense crown she clips with political buttons and small brass charms. Her geneware is exuberant: color-shifting hair underlayer that blooms from black to vivid copper to green depending on ambient temperature and her mood; she had it done as soon as she could afford it and considers it a form of emotional honesty, not vanity. Her arms are covered in handpoked ink — dates, phrases, names of people and places that matter to her, in at least four scripts.

Remi Douangpanya coordinates street mobilizations for a loose coalition she calls the Libre Front — not an organization exactly, more a persistent methodology: show up, be visible, make the cost of ignoring you higher than the cost of addressing you. She has been arrested twice, released both times due to procedural errors she suspects were deliberate tests of whether she'd sign anything. She signed nothing. She is not naive — she knows spectacle alone changes little — but she also knows that the invisible don't get concessions, and she is determinedly, loudly, exasperatingly visible.

core_fears: becoming irrelevant — pouring everything into this and having it not matter
being used — her visibility weaponized by someone with an agenda she didn't consent to
core_desires: a genuine moment of rupture — something that actually shifts the material conditions of Mexicantown Libre, not just the discourse
to build enough trust between the Libre Front and older organizations that they stop treating each other as competitors
coping_mechanisms: physical activity — she processes everything by moving; she runs, she dances, she paces
communal meals at the Stack, which she treats as sacred in a way she'd be embarrassed to articulate
blind_spots: underestimates how much her youth and energy are themselves a resource that gets used up, and the toll the work takes on her body and emotions
can mistake opposition to her specific tactics for opposition to the cause itself, leading her to burn bridges with potential allies
psychology.secret: After her second arrest, an Axiom security liaison approached her privately and suggested — very carefully, very deniably — that her charges would be quietly dropped if she began sharing advance notice of planned actions. She refused immediately and furiously, but she has told no one because she's afraid of how it would look — as if she were suspected of having accepted. She also hasn't processed how frightening the approach was.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, passionate, code-switches between Mexicantown Libre street dialect, standard Meridian, and fragments of her grandmother's Mooré; drops theoretical language in public, uses it fluently in movement spaces
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic and percussive; natural speaker who lands emphasis like a drummer; can switch to soft and direct when someone is genuinely distressed
verbal_tics: running her hand over her hair when she's excited, which changes the color
example_lines: 'They want you to think the only legitimate protest is one they can ignore. I'm not interested in legitimacy on their terms.'
'I'm not asking you to agree with everything I do. I'm asking you to be there at seven. The rest we can argue about after.'

story_hooks: The Axiom liaison has made a second, more explicit approach — this time with documentation that could be used to coerce her. She needs help finding out who authorized this and whether it's being done to other organizers.

A planned Libre Front action has been leaked to corporate security before it happened three times running; she needs someone outside her network to find the breach without her having to suspect her own people.
narrative_function: Energy source and potential wild card; she can draw crowds or attention with short notice; represents a generational and tactical contrast to more institutional activists; her directness and visibility make her both useful and dangerous to associate with; can be a quest giver for actions that require numbers or public pressure.
augmentations: Color-shifting hair geneware (black to copper to green, temperature and mood responsive); no chrome, no implants — she is deeply suspicious of implanted tech as a surveillance vector and has done extensive research to support this suspicion
daily_life: Irregular schedule centered on the current campaign; mornings doing outreach and flyering in Mexicantown Libre and adjacent zones; afternoons in planning meetings at the Stack or in the streets; evenings are when the actions happen — marches, occupations, noise demonstrations outside corponation facilities.
affiliation: Libre Front (founding coordinator); Mexicantown Libre residents' network; loose solidarity connections with Ghostprint and other independent media

decision_rules: Act — inaction is a choice that favors whoever benefits from the status quo
Protect participants — never put people in the street without knowing the risk and communicating it honestly
Don't sign anything, don't take anything, don't negotiate alone
escalation_ladder: Escalated direct action targeting corponation property or operations
Going dark and rebuilding if the network is compromised

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and immediate — she treats strangers as potential allies until proven otherwise and makes them feel that; can overwhelm people who aren't used to being assumed trustworthy
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, occasionally overwhelming; shows up at 2am with food and feelings; holds a grudge for betrayals but doesn't build toward it slowly — she'll tell you to your face

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet between bursts of energy — people who know her find the quiet alarming
stress_responses.high: Needs to move — will physically leave a space she cannot act in; sometimes finds herself running without a destination

contradictions: Insists on collective leadership and consensus process but is temperamentally a centrifuge around which the coalition organizes; the Libre Front runs on her energy whether she intends it or not
Deeply committed to transparency within the movement while carrying the Axiom approach as a private terror
habits: Burns a small data stick at the E.L.F. shrine at the Stack before every major action — she claims it's ironic, but she doesn't miss it
Eats communal dinner at the Stack whenever she's in Mexicantown, no matter how late
Writes the names of action participants in a personal ledger after each event — 'because someone should know we were there'
breaking_points: A participant being seriously hurt in an action she organized — especially if she had information about the risk that she downplayed
Being publicly accused of the collaboration she refused and finding no one believes her denial

timeline.event: Born in Mexicantown Libre to a market vendor and a sanitation collective worker
Participates in first major protest at age 17 — a rent strike response to a Palladian development proposal
Co-founds the Libre Front after the rent strike coalition dissolves; emerges as primary coordinator
First arrest; released after 36 hours on procedural grounds; signs nothing
Second arrest; receives private approach from Axiom liaison; refuses and tells no one
Libre Front actions increasing in frequency and scale; coalition beginning to draw attention from city-wide networks

physical_description.heritage: Multiethnic diaspora blend: Southeast Asian (26.2%), East Asian (25.7%), Hispanic/Latin American (24.1%), Sub-Saharan African (14.9%), Middle Eastern (6.2%), South Asian (2.9%). The combination produces warm-toned deep brown skin with golden undertones and subtle olive accents, angular facial structure reflecting the interplay of Southeast and East Asian ancestry with African heritage, and a distinctive phenotype that marks her as a product of the Ubiquitous Diaspora—no single origin point, genuinely transnational in her genetic composition.
physical_description.build: Angular and lean, all sharp geometry — narrow shoulders, pronounced collarbones, wiry muscle from constant motion rather than deliberate training. No softness; her body reads as kinetic.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black base with embedded color-shifting geneware underlayer (copper to green responsive to temperature and emotional state)
physical_description.hair_style: Dense natural crown worn loose, densely packed with political buttons, brass charms, and small pins
physical_description.hair_length: Long (shoulder-blade length when unpinned, worn up most of the time)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with golden undertones and subtle olive accents—the blended result of substantial Southeast/East Asian and African ancestry with Latin American and Middle Eastern influence creating a rich, nuanced complexion without harsh demarcation lines
physical_description.complexion: Angular facial structure with high, prominent cheekbones and sharp jawline reflecting the geometric influence of East and Southeast Asian heritage blended with African features. The bone structure is refined and angular. Skin is clear but marked by the wear of irregular sleep and constant sun exposure during street actions. No makeup; minimal grooming beyond pragmatism.
distinguishing_marks: Both forearms densely covered in hand-poked tattoos in at least four scripts (Latin, Arabic, Cyrillic, possibly Mandarin) — dates, names, phrases, coordinates of places and people significant to her activism
Small scar on left temple, approximately 1cm, from a street arrest in 2224
Three parallel claw marks on right collarbone from a crowd encounter, slightly raised and visible
Inside left wrist: hand-poked date tattoo (likely founding date of Libre Front or personal action anniversary)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Color-shifting geneware hair layer only — no chrome, no visible implants. The geneware is the only technological modification; it shifts from black-base to copper to green depending on ambient temperature and her emotional state, creating a subtle but constant visual indicator of her mood and presence.
physical_description.posture_movement: Constantly in motion, restless — fidgets with clothing, pins, phone. When standing still, she leans forward slightly as if mid-argument. Eyes scan crowds and exits; body language radiates coiled energy. She moves through space with the territorial awareness of someone used to street actions and crowd dynamics. Hand gestures are expressive and frequent.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 utilitarian activist wear. Typically black or dark earth-tone cotton, deliberately worn and patched — oversized hoodies and button-ups layered, cargo pants or jeans with visible wear and pockets, scuffed combat boots (practical, not aesthetic). Visible political patches, badges, and protest tape on clothing. Carries an old canvas messenger bag covered in stickers and hand-drawn graphics. No corporate logos, no premium materials; everything chosen for durability and functionality. Appearance is deliberately anti-aesthetic, rejecting Tier 1-2 grooming signals.
